sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Wichita Falls?
sections.html:
Three kinds of offices touch a Wichita Falls tax bill. The Wichita Appraisal District sets values and handles exemptions and protests. The City of Wichita Falls, Wichita County and the school district set their own rates. The Wichita County Tax Office sends the bills and takes payment. It collects for 8 taxing jurisdictions and disbursed almost $120 million in its latest tax year.

Wichita Falls has 101,951 residents, a little below the 2010 count of 104,553. The median home value is $156,800, which matters for taxes: the $140,000 school exemption removes most of the school district value on a typical house here.

  • Values, exemptions, protests: Wichita Appraisal District, P.O. Box 5172, Wichita Falls, 76307, phone (940) 322-2435, weekdays 8:00am to 5:00pm.
  • Bills and payment: Wichita County Tax Office.
  • City budget and rate hearings: the City of Wichita Falls.

For 2026 the city adopted $0.677900 per $100 of taxable value, down from $0.682500 the year before. Wichita County adopted $0.518590 and Wichita Falls ISD adopted $1.034677. Rates for neighboring towns in the county moved in different directions, so a seller comparing nearby markets should look at the whole bill, school district included.

The city rate has two pieces: $0.652925 for maintenance and operations and $0.024975 for debt. Its no-new-revenue rate is $0.666037 and its voter-approval rate is $0.717729. A rate above the no-new-revenue figure raises more money from the same properties than last year. A rate below the voter-approval figure needs no election. The city sits between the two. The school district carries a big debt share of its own, $0.359277 of the $1.034677.

Burkburnett city moved from $0.678251 to $0.758386, while Iowa Park held at $0.694500 for both years. The combined rate on your own account comes from the county tax office.

Wichita Falls tax is due by January 31. A balance still open on February 1 turns delinquent under Texas law, and that day brings a 6% penalty plus 1% interest. The penalty then gains a point every month and stops at 12% on July 1. Interest keeps running with no ceiling. Owners who are seniors, disabled, or disabled veteran homeowners may split the bill into four payments.

  • Early spring: the appraisal district mails notices of appraised value, starting around April 1 for single-family homesteads.
  • May 15: protest deadline in most years, with a later cutoff if notices arrive late.
  • July 25: the chief appraiser certifies the roll to each taxing unit.
  • October: bills go out, and tax is due on receipt.
  • January 31: last day before late charges begin.

The tax office follows the Wichita Falls ISD schedule for weather closures, so check before driving downtown on a bad-weather day near the deadline.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and other ways to lower the bill
sections.html:
Two moves do most of the work: file for the residence homestead exemption and protest the appraisal if the value looks high. Both go through the appraisal district, and exemption applications generally must be filed before May 1.

Every residence homestead gets a $140,000 break on the school district value, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000. Nothing applies by itself in most cases: you file, and the chief appraiser decides whether the property qualifies. Counties, cities and colleges may add their own percentage or dollar exemptions, so ask the appraisal district what the city and county have adopted.

  • Disabled veteran exemptions run from $5,000 for a rating of 10% to 29% up to $12,000 for 70% to 100%. A veteran rated 100% disabled can receive a total exemption on a residence homestead.
  • A homestead appraisal cannot rise more than 10% a year once the exemption has been in place for a year.
  • Seniors and disabled owners can freeze the school district tax on their home.
  • A surviving spouse age 55 or older may keep a deceased spouse's over-65 benefits in certain cases.

An owner who loses at the review board can go on to district court or binding arbitration, and keeps paying the undisputed tax in the meantime.

The city rate has drifted down: $0.694321 for 2022, $0.680000 for 2023, $0.684800 for 2024, $0.682500 for 2025 and $0.677900 for 2026. Wichita Falls ISD fell faster, from $1.296500 in 2022 to $1.034677 in 2026, and Wichita County slid from $0.560400 to $0.518590.

With all three rates falling, a bigger bill almost always means a higher taxable value, not a higher rate. The homestead cap holds that increase to 10% a year on a qualifying home, and it applies only to homesteads.

Before you list, make one call: if your notice of appraised value jumped by more than the cap allows, ask the appraisal district at (940) 322-2435 whether the homestead exemption is on file. A missing exemption leaves the full school value on the bill.

The tax lien starts January 1, so the year's tax is settled from the seller's side at closing. Liability for the year sits with the January 1 owner, even on a March sale. Unpaid tax on the account blocks clear title for the buyer.

  1. Before listing, ask the county tax office for a statement from each taxing unit.
  2. Hand the statements to the title company so it can total any balance.
  3. Pay what is owed from the sale proceeds at closing.
  4. Keep the receipt for your records.

Heirs of an inherited house who are not named on the recorded deed can claim the exemption with an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a utility bill.

If taxes go delinquent, the collector sends notices, may offer a payment plan, and can sue. Court costs are added to the bill. Tax foreclosure sales are auctions run by the constable or an agent the unit hires. Texas gives former owners a limited right to redeem, with a longer window for homestead, agricultural and mineral property.

Back taxes do not rule out a sale. The title company pays the balance from your proceeds at closing, and the buyer receives a clean account. A cash sale skips the lender appraisal and repair requests, which helps when time is short. Call the tax office for a payoff figure first. Then you know the full delinquent amount, with penalty and interest, before you weigh any offer. If the account has gone to a lawsuit, ask whether a payment plan is on file and bring that paper to the title company too.

faqs.q: What is the Wichita Falls city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: $0.677900 per $100 of taxable value, adopted by the city. It was $0.682500 for tax year 2025.

faqs.q: When are Wichita County property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1. Anything unpaid then picks up a 6% penalty and 1% interest, and the penalty climbs each month to 12% in July.
The Wichita Appraisal District, at (940) 322-2435 or cs@wadtx.com, weekdays 8:00am to 5:00pm. Call it about values, exemptions and protests.

faqs.q: How much school exemption does a homestead get?
faqs.a: $140,000 off the school district value on a residence homestead, plus another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners. You must apply, usually before May 1.

faqs.q: Did Wichita Falls rates go down this year?
faqs.a: Yes, for the city, county and school district. The city went from 0.682500 to 0.677900 and Wichita Falls ISD from 1.075287 to 1.034677.
